A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ACDiT and are readable throughout. The retained methods, equations, experiments, and visual examples can be matched across reorganization, including material relocated into v3 Appendices A–E.

before.justification: v2 reports original ImageNet generation and classification results, UCF-101 generation results, and ablation, scaling, and timing analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and additionally reports OpenWebText results, expanded ablations, and inference-time comparisons with MAR.

M1.justification: v3 adds a text adaptation using discrete diffusion objectives and discrete-token corruption and denoising during training and inference. The visual method, SCAM attention pattern, blockwise autoregression, RoPE-ND, and clean-context caching remain unchanged; the new appendix code documents existing components.

E1.justification: v3 adds text modeling on OpenWebText, extending actual evaluation beyond continuous visual data to a distinct modality and task. ImageNet generation/classification and 16-frame UCF-101 generation remain covered.

E2.justification: v3 adds AR, SEDD, MDLM, and BD3-LMs to the new text comparison, Video-LaVIT and MagDiff to the UCF-101 comparison, and MAR-B/MAR-L to a new timing comparison. The image-generation comparator set is retained: MAR-L-Causal renames the existing causal MAR-L row.

E3.justification: v3 introduces text evaluation using validation perplexity and variational likelihood bounds, plus a controlled 4096-token MAR timing comparison. The positional ablation changes from FID-10K through 400K training steps to FID-50K through 500K steps. Main visual-training settings are retained; these disclosures do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 6b expands the positional ablation to test standard 1D-RoPE and replacement of clean context with noisy context, directly examining two central design choices. Table 6 adds an efficiency analysis against MAR. Existing block-size, scaling, and WSD analyses remain.

E5.justification: v3 introduces no seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and retains the existing uncertainty-reporting practice. The new perplexity upper bounds express variational likelihood bounds rather than statistical confidence intervals.

E6.justification: New results include an ACDiT perplexity upper bound of 21.59 at L'=8 in Table 4 and timing results in Table 6: ACDiT-L reports 2.29s/4.08s for image/long-sequence workloads versus MAR-L's 3.58s/63.82s. Video baseline rows and revised ablation curves are also added. Retained main image, video, and classification scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 1 corrects the autoregressive factorization from a product predicting x_(i+1) to a product of p(x_i|x_<i), fixing its indexing. The FLOPS derivation relocated to Appendix A is algebraically equivalent to v2 Section 4.3; the reformulation and standard perplexity formula do not constitute new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the demonstrated contribution from image/video generation to image, video, and text, adding a claim of strong text performance without specialized customization. The central claims about blockwise visual generation, KV-cache efficiency, and transfer to visual understanding remain.

C2.justification: v3 attributes text performance to its positional encoding, recommends blocks spanning 2–4 video frames, and identifies adaptive block sizing as future work. It qualifies the MAR long-sequence comparison as a computational proxy because MAR is not video-trained. Appendix B newly notes that target-dataset tokenizer training might improve results.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds substantial implementation examples for SCAM construction, FlexAttention, cached attention, and conditional transformer blocks. v3 also specifies the text backbone and clarifies that the visual tokenizer is not further trained. Most visual hyperparameters and hardware details move to Appendix B, although the explicit MAE fine-tuning recipe reference and positional-ablation patch-size statement disappear.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused positioning against Block Diffusion and references supporting discrete text diffusion, OpenWebText, and the added video baselines. It also adds Ha and Schmidhuber's World Models and removes the Radford et al. (2019) and Ko et al. (2023) references. The existing related-work organization and principal visual-generation positioning remain.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the introductory motivation and expands the method exposition. Desiderata move from prerequisites into the method section, implementation material is reorganized between Section 4.5 and Appendix B, and the detailed efficiency derivation moves to Appendix A. The new appendix structure substantially reorganizes the document beyond routine language corrections.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column formatting to a single-column TMLR layout. Figure 1 adds AR/DiT comparisons, Figure 3 expands and combines method-comparison and architecture diagrams, and the ablation plot is redrawn. New text/timing tables appear, classification gains a parameter column, and the existing image/video samples are merged into Appendix E Figure 7.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, v3 provides more direct tests of clean-context and positional-encoding choices, a MAR timing comparison, and inspectable implementation examples. These strengthen support and transparency, while OpenWebText adds useful generality evidence. The gains are limited by partly specified text/timing protocols, omissions of some earlier recipe details, and illustrative code containing a syntax typo; the central visual findings remain unchanged.
